thread:
sara: support escalation — multiple customers reporting p95/p99 spike for text.generate after the runtime rollout (~1.2) at 03:12 UTC. Some requests hit 30s timeout. linking dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/xyz/latency
mike: oncall runtime — thanks. which regions/models show the spike?
elaine: looking — spike is concentrated in us-west and europe, heavy on `redwood-7b` and `redwood-13b` variants. traces show tail increased around request queuing, not token generation. histogram: p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 820ms (was 410ms), p99 ~ 2.6s (was 1.1s).
karthik: question: did the rollout include the kernel-selector change + new batching heuristics?
deploy-bot: deploy event: runtime/1.2.0 rolled to prod at 2025-11-12T03:12:08Z by ci-cd (id: dpl-202511120312). canary cohort: 2% for 10m, then progressive.
tyler: I see sidecar CPU saturation on several nodes in us-west-2 around 03:15 UTC. queue length on hotpath increased ~3x. suspect new batching config increased CPU on sidecars (packetization).
mike: can we repro in staging? any quick config we can toggle to isolate batching vs kernel change?
karthik: yes — two quick experiments: 1) disable new batcher (fallback to legacy packer) 2) pin kernel selector to pre-1.2 rule. Both are hotpatchable on canary pool.
elaine: logs show most latency is spent in wait_for_worker + enqueue time. sample snippet:```
[2025-11-12T03:15:21Z] request_id=xyz enqueue_ms=210 worker_acquire_ms=340 exec_ms=40 total_ms=610
[2025-11-12T03:15:22Z] request_id=abc enqueue_ms=820 worker_acquire_ms=140 exec_ms=60 total_ms=1020
```
sara: customers asking for ETA — can we provide a mitigated rollback or config toggle quickly?
tyler: immediate mitigation: reduce max_batch_size to 8 and lower batch_window_ms to 8 on prod canaries. will push to 5% canary first. command:```
# patch canary runtime config
redwoodctl runtime patch --pool canary --param max_batch_size=8 --param batch_window_ms=8 --env prod --apply
```
mike: doing bisect plan: 1) apply patch to canary pool, measure p95 for 10m 2) if improvement, roll patch wider 3) if no improvement, rollback to runtime/1.1.9 on canary and test 4) if regression disappears on rollback, schedule full rollback.
deploy-bot: patch applied to canary at 2025-11-12T03:28:05Z (target=5%).
elaine: after patch p95 on canary dropped from 790ms -> 420ms in ~8m. p99 dropped from 2.5s -> 1.0s. staging repro with same load shows similar delta when toggling batcher.
karthik: that points to batching heuristics. root cause hypothesis: new batch aggregation increases sidecar CPU spikes for short sequences causing head-of-line blocking. will open a short PR to throttle batch size under high queue depth and favor worker preemption.
tyler: for immediate customer relief, increasing sidecar replicas + rate-limit slow customers at edge is low-risk. Ops command:```
kubectl scale deployment sidecar-us-west --replicas=6 -n runtime-prod
```
sara: I'll notify support to message affected customers: "We identified a batching heuristic in the recent runtime rollout causing queuing; engineers have applied a canary patch and are monitoring. We'll follow up with timeline for a full rollout or rollback." :thumbsup:
mike: ongoing watch — monitoring dashboards and traces. if p99 back to normal for 30m, we'll promote patch to 25% then 100%.
elaine: adding an evaluation alert rule for enqueue_ms > 300ms to trigger page next time.
karthik: creating changelog + postmortem stub now; tagging runtime/batching and rollout process. action items: (1) tune heuristics (PR), (2) add canary perf gate for enqueue_ms, (3) automated rollback on 2x p95 increase during rollout.
sara: customers updated. I'll keep this thread for status. thanks team.
mike: update 03:58 UTC — canary p95 stable at ~420ms, p99 at ~980ms. promoting to 25% now.
tyler: scaling sidecars back to baseline after promotion looks fine.
sara: closing loop with support, opening incident ticket for postmortem. end of thread.
